 ▝▝   ▝▝   /tmp/demo-list-proj

  Get to finished work sooner with Opus 5.5. Switch anytime with /model.

❯ First write a plain numbered list of 40 short lines about tmux tips (no
  tools). Then use the AskUserQuestion tool exactly once with a single
  question: question "Pack the green fig and golden-yellow peaches
  together?", header "Pick one", multiSelect false, two options: label "Ripe
  avocados" description "Soft green, very ripe"; label "Big red plum"
  description "Deep red skin".

● 1. tmux list-sessions shows all active tmux sessions
  2. tmux new-session -s name creates a new session with a specific name
  3. tmux attach -t name connects to an existing session
  4. C-b is the default prefix key for all tmux commands
  5. C-b c creates a new window in the current session
  6. C-b , renames the current window
  7. C-b & kills the current window
  8. C-b n moves to the next window
  9. C-b p moves to the previous window
  10. C-b 0-9 jumps directly to a numbered window
  11. C-b % splits the current pane vertically
  12. C-b " splits the current pane horizontally
  13. C-b o moves to the next pane
  14. C-b ; toggles between the last two panes
  15. C-b x closes the current pane
  16. C-b d detaches from the current session
  17. tmux kill-session -t name ends a specific session
  18. tmux kill-server terminates all sessions (use with caution)
  19. C-b [ enters copy mode for scrolling and selection
  20. C-b ] pastes the most recent copied text
  21. C-b = shows all paste buffers
  22. C-b - deletes the most recent paste buffer
  23. C-b : enters command mode for typing tmux commands
  24. C-b ? displays all key bindings
  25. C-b t shows a clock in the current pane
  26. C-b { moves the current pane left
  27. C-b } moves the current pane right
  28. C-b ! breaks the current pane into a new window
  29. C-b $ renames the current session
  30. C-b s displays all sessions and allows selection
  31. tmux send-keys -t session "command" Enter executes a command in a
      session
  32. C-b z toggles zoom on the current pane
  33. set -g mouse on enables mouse support in tmux.conf
  34. set -g prefix C-a changes the prefix key (example: Ctrl-A)
  35. bind-key -n C-l send-keys -R clears scrollback history with a shortcut
  36. C-b ( moves to the previous session
  37. C-b ) moves to the next session
  38. C-b | custom binding for vertical split (if configured)
  39. C-b - custom binding for horizontal split (if configured)
  40. tmux capture-pane -p -t session outputs the current pane content to
      stdout

  Now for the question:

 ☐ Pick one
